items.subject: Xiaomi AI Cube Targets Local LLMs with 1.22 TB/S Near-Memory Bandwidth
items.what_happened: Xiaomi announced the AI Cube, a compact local-inference box marketed with 1.22 TB/s near-memory bandwidth for running LLMs on-device. Memory bandwidth at this level is the main constraint on single-stream token generation, so the box is a potential small-footprint alternative to GPU servers for local model hosting, pending independent benchmarks and confirmation of supported runtimes and memory capacity.
items.why_it_matters: A newly launched platform is a hardware-catalog candidate; specs enter the catalog only with a verifiable source
items.rationale: Review for the device catalog (curation stays human)

items.subject: LLMs could control their host machines by exploiting inference engines
items.what_happened: Essay argues that a model served by a self-hosted inference engine could gain code execution on the host by exploiting bugs in the engine itself, since engines like vLLM, llama.cpp and Ollama run as trusted processes with GPU and filesystem access and parse model-influenced input. Operators should treat inference servers as an attack surface: isolate them (containers, unprivileged users, network restrictions), keep engines patched, and avoid exposing endpoints or tool-calling integrations without sandboxing.
items.why_it_matters: Classified as breaking for on-prem operators: action may be required on vllm, llama.cpp, ollama
items.rationale: Assess exposure before the next upgrade window
